column1: # #1023 A/B shared oracle, measured with Java (NamedCapture / SemanticPredicateParser / CaptureBoundaryParser.input).
# A collector (Chain, Optional, ZeroOrMore, SyncPointRecoveryParser, NonOrdered) returns what it collected in the consumed kind:
# a MatchOnly child contributes nothing, a host projection is collected in order (Rust: Sequence, optional_java,
# repeat_java, recover, NonOrdered). Input: prefix + "c" with prefix "" / "p" / "😀\r\n" (column 1 is its CP length).
# Shapes: MO = MatchOnly('c'), &c = PEG lookahead, proj / proj0 = a host projection "Z" / "" whose logical start
# is 0 (it consumes nothing), projc = "Z" that consumes one code point, projm = "Z" of the matchOnly kind, vc = 'c'
# returned in the virtualTokenConsumed kind; other atoms are words; Rep = ZeroOrMore, Rec = recovery with sync
# token ";", Ord = NonOrdered. Rule[X] is a referenced rule with body X, as UBNF generates it (Java: a LazyChoice of a
# Choice body's alternatives, a LazyChain of a Chain body's elements, else a single-element LazyChain, so a body that
# is only a rule reference, Rule[Rule[X]], is one too; Rust: Expr::Rule of a rule with that body).
# capture/cursor: prefix NamedCapture("w", X) observed after X (provenance@CP span'text', consumed/matched), then
# Replay("w") and full input ("unreached": X failed). candidate/failure/acceptC/acceptNotC: prefix predicate(X) 'c'
# whose callback accepts exactly "c" / exactly not "c" ("~" is empty text). field: prefix input boundary(X) span
# ("G" generated, "fail" rejected or X failed). Rust reads every row at the full-input entry, the same entry with a
# .stop_consume() root, ParseContext::parse and the explicit Classic entry; both languages use memo 2 x diagnostics 3.
